name: com.eurorackref/eurorack
description: Eurorack module reference: typed jacks, controls, modes and specs, cited to manufacturer documents.

tools.name: search_modules
tools.description:
Find Eurorack modules: by name, by a combination of filters, or resolve a whole list of names to ids at once.

Filters compose with AND. Omit any filter to leave that dimension unrestricted. Results are sorted by module name; use limit/offset to page.

Args:
  - names (string[]): resolve up to 100 module names to ids in one call — the way a user writes their rack ("Maths", "Plaits", "Pamela's New Workout", "Morph 4"). Use this instead of one search per name. Can't be combined with other filters; returns { resolutions, _meta } instead of { modules, total } (see below).
  - function_tag (string): what the module does, from a fixed vocabulary (e.g. looping_envelope, slew_limiter, lowpass_gate, granular, sub_oscillator). The strongest way to search by function. By default it matches only PATCHABLE functions — ones you can patch an external signal through or whose result is on an output jack. Pass include_internal: true to also match functions that only shape the module's own sound (e.g. a voice's built-in low-pass gate).
  - jack_type (string): the module has a jack of this standard type (e.g. end_of_cycle_out, pitch_cv_in, sync_in, audio_in_left).
  - block_type (string): the module has an internal block of this type (e.g. envelope_generator, vca, filter, delay).
  - manufacturer (string): manufacturer id, e.g. 'make-noise', 'mutable-instruments'. Exact match; a near-miss returns _meta.manufacturer_suggestions.
  - hp_min, hp_max (number): module width in HP.
  - power_plus_12_max (number): +12 V draw at most this many mA (modules with a stated draw only).
  - has_modes (boolean): true = the module has selectable modes (per its record); false = it has none.
  - signal_type_in (string): the module has an input jack carrying this signal: audio, cv, pitch (V/oct), gate, trigger, clock or midi. 'cv' also matches pitch jacks. A bidirectional jack counts as an input and an output.
  - signal_type_out (string): the module has an output jack carrying this signal. Same values.
  - text (string): case-insensitive match against module id, name, slug and curated aliases. Separator- and whitespace-insensitive ("filter 8" finds "filter-8", "3x MIA" finds "3xMIA"). Names only — search by what a module does with function_tag / jack_type / block_type.
  - voct_tracking_range_min (number): the manufacturer states a pitch tracking range of at least this many octaves.
  - audio_outputs_min (number): has at least this many audio output jacks (e.g. ≥3 finds multi-output filters).
    Every filter except manufacturer, hp, power and text reads the modules' typed records. A few modules have no record yet; _meta.record_coverage gives the count when it matters, so say when a result may be incomplete.
  - limit (number): default 50, max 200. offset (number): pagination offset.

Returns (filters):
  {
    "modules": [{ id, name, manufacturer { id, name }, hp, function_tags, production_status, url }],  // function_tags: the record's function tag ids, [] without a record
    "total": number,
    "_meta": {
      "query": <args>,
      "record_coverage": { with_record, total, note },  // when a record-backed filter was used
      "relaxed_to_tokens": true,                         // a multi-word phrase matched nothing, so each word was matched against identifiers instead
      // On total=0 only, each optional:
      "would_match_without": ["text"],                   // filters that, if individually dropped, would yield ≥1 result
      "closest_text_hits": [{ id, name, manufacturer }], // top 3 modules matching 'text' alone
      "did_you_mean": [{ id, name, manufacturer }],      // edit-distance neighbors of 'text' (typo); absent means a genuine corpus gap
      "manufacturer_suggestions": [{ id, name }],        // maker slugs near the 'manufacturer' arg
      "feedback_hint": "..."
    }
  }

Examples:
  - "Looping envelopes with an end-of-cycle output" → {function_tag: 'looping_envelope', jack_type: 'end_of_cycle_out'}
  - "What ALM modules are in the corpus?" → {manufacturer: 'alm-busy-circuits'}
  - "Modules under 8 HP with a clock output" → {hp_max: 8, signal_type_out: 'clock'}
  - "Filters that track V/Oct over 5 octaves" → {voct_tracking_range_min: 5}
  - "Multi-output filters" → {audio_outputs_min: 3, text: 'filter'}

Returns (names):
  {
    "resolutions": [{ input, best_match (a module card or null), score (0..1), match_kind ('id'|'slug'|'exact'|'relaxed'|'ambiguous'|'fuzzy'|'none'), did_you_mean [cards], ambiguous [cards] }],
    "_meta": { requested, resolved, feedback_hint? }
  }
  If a name is ambiguous, show the user the candidates; don't pick one. best_match null with nothing in did_you_mean means the module isn't in the reference.

After picking a hit, call get_module with the id (or module_ids for several) for full details.

names.description: Module names (or ids) to resolve, up to 100. Order and duplicates preserved. Not combinable with filters.

include_internal.description: With function_tag: also match functions that act only inside the module (no patch point). Default false.

power_plus_12_max.description: +12 V draw at most this many mA.

tools.name: get_module
tools.description:
Return the citation-anchored specification for one Eurorack module by id, or for up to 25 at once.

Use it when you know the module id (from search_modules) and want its specs: HP, depth, power, and the typed record — jacks (direction, signals, voltages, what they feed or come from), controls, modes, hidden functions, specs with units, properties, behavior rules and function tags — plus its manufacturer documents and firmware history.

Module ids are "<manufacturer-id>/<module-slug>", e.g. "make-noise/maths". A near-miss id (missing maker, wrong maker, known alias) resolves; _meta.id_resolved_from says so.

Args (exactly one of module_id / module_ids):
  - module_id: one id → returns the module.
  - module_ids: up to 25 ids → returns { modules: [...], errors: [{ id, message }] }; one bad id doesn't fail the batch. Prefer this over repeated calls.
  - view: "concise" returns the id card (name, manufacturer, hp, function_tags, production_status, url) without the record — the cheapest way to triage a list. "full" (default) returns everything. Ignored when fields is set.
  - fields: top-level keys to include (e.g. ["record"], ["power"]). id and _meta are always returned. Takes precedence over view.

Returns (per module):
  - id, name, manufacturer { id, name }, hp, depth_mm, power { plus_12, minus_12, plus_5 } (mA), production_status ("current" | "discontinued")
  - function_tags: the record's function tag ids, a quick "what does it do"
  - url: the module's page on eurorackref.com
  - record: the typed record, or null when the module hasn't been extracted yet (then _meta.feedback_hint says so). Layers: blocks[] (named circuits with their controls/inputs/outputs and types), jacks[] (name, direction input|output|bidirectional, signal_types, function, voltage_min/max, polarity, scaling, threshold_v, pulse_ms, coupling, audio_rate, impedance_ohms, normalled_from, attenuated_by, feeds / sourced_from / selected_by, per_mode, types, not_stated, name_basis), controls[] (function, range, positions, affects, per_mode, name_basis), modes[], hidden_functions[], specs[] (quantity, min/max/value, unit, condition), properties[] (subject/property/value), rules[] (subject / when / effect, optional mode), tags[] (tag, basis, evidence, scope). Every element cites src, a source id listed in sources. Labels are the manual's own terms, never quotes. name_basis says whether a name is printed on the panel, described in the docs, or inferred. A field listed in a jack's not_stated was checked and the manufacturer doesn't state it; a null field not listed there is unknown.
  - sources[]: { id, source_type, format, title, canonical_url (the manufacturer's URL), url (its page here), last_verified, canonical_changed_at, primary?, changed_since_verified? }. Cite canonical_url. changed_since_verified means the manufacturer's document changed after we last checked it — say so when it matters.
  - firmware_versions[]: { version, release_date, notes, source_id }
  - _meta: last_verified, record_meta { schema_version, extracted_at }, feedback_hint, id_resolved_from

Errors: "Module not found: <id>" (with did-you-mean suggestions) for a single unknown id.

If the manufacturer's documents don't cover the question, say so — never infer from spec data.

module_ids.description: Up to 25 module ids; returns { modules, errors }.

view.description: "concise" returns the id card without the record. "full" (default) returns everything. Ignored when `fields` is set.

fields.description: Top-level keys to include. id and _meta are always returned. Selectable: manufacturer, name, hp, depth_mm, power, production_status, function_tags, url, record, sources, firmware_versions.

tools.name: get_manufacturer
tools.description:
Return one Eurorack manufacturer: its website, every module of theirs in the reference, and their maker-wide documents.

Use it for "what does <maker> make?" or to browse a maker's line before picking modules. For filtering (by function, jacks, HP) use search_modules with manufacturer instead.

Args:
  - manufacturer_id: the maker's id, e.g. "make-noise", "mutable-instruments", "alm-busy-circuits". A near-miss returns an error listing close ids.

Returns:
  - id, name, website (the maker's own site), url (their page on eurorackref.com)
  - module_count, modules[]: { id, name, manufacturer, hp, function_tags, production_status, url }, by name
  - sources[]: maker-wide documents not tied to one module (same shape as get_module's sources)
  - _meta.corpus_records: how many modules in the whole reference have a typed record
